assets: maintainer GitHub identity and release credentials
npm tarballs and GitHub Packages mirror
boundaries: fork or pull request to repository
build job to attestation and signing
release workflow to npm and GitHub Release

threats.threat: An attacker impersonates a maintainer and changes protected workflow or release settings.
threats.residual: GitHub account recovery remains an external identity risk.

threats.threat: A dependency or build step injects unreviewed code into the release artifact.
threats.residual: Shared hosted runners and network-enabled build steps prevent a full SLSA L3 isolation claim.

threats.threat: A producer denies building or publishing a specific artifact.
threats.residual: The current VSA verifier identity belongs to the same project.

threats.threat: Secrets, internal records, or unlicensed content are packaged into a release.
threats.residual: Human review is still required for semantic confidentiality mistakes.

threats.threat: A compromised or unavailable upstream prevents reproducible release and recovery.
threats.residual: There is no organization-controlled binary artifact proxy.

threats.threat: An untrusted pull request obtains a write token or publishing capability.
threats.residual: Platform workflow semantics must remain under update review.

threats.threat: A release artifact or SBOM is replaced after build.
controls: signature subjects include tarballs and SBOMs
threats.residual: Consumers must actually run the verification commands.

review_triggers: security advisory affecting build or distribution
